intro: The forty-eighth screen read 102 pictures, the set's 21 and 81 probes, with thirteen readers and four scorers: 1,067 of 1,114 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **All 64 templates pass the legibility gate, the two that failed in v0.50 among them.** `play_catch`, with the ball drawn early on its path, reads 1.00 in five pictures, and the thrower is the thrower in all five. The ball's place was measured before it was built: v0.50's two failing pictures were built again in three arms and read blind, and the girl was read as the thrower in 3 readings of 8 as screened and in 7 of 8 with the ball early. `square_wheel`, with no hose by the barrow, reads 1.00 in eight pictures, four of them the barrow. The bread for the ducks, a slice now in the feeder's hand, and the lost balloon, its string's end clear of the fence's rails and of the pond, read 1.00 in five pictures each. Of the 47 items under full marks, 44 are the clouds or a tree, left out by a reader; the other three are half marks, two on the stopped hose in one picture and one on an ice cream. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. The set's score rose to 0.976 from 0.949. A full gate is not the end of the reading: many full marks carry a hedge, and on the strict count 56 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.50's 52. And the grown figures are called young first in 5 of their 85 pictures, for 3 of 79: a wider moustache for the man in the red shirt was benched and changed nothing, and he is a boy when he sweeps.
design:
## Design tests

The cast of builder 0.51.0 and revision 48's rules were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v051.md`, eight pictures, one fresh reader each). The bench had read each change on its own or in v0.50's own pictures; here a reader has them at a picture's size. Between them the eight forced sets hold the game of catch four times, the square wheel four times (three barrows and a bicycle), the lost balloon three times, and the bread for the ducks and the fence painter twice each. Six placed on their first seed, one on its second, and one on its sixty-fourth: a game of catch beside the pond with a duck feeder and a picnic. I looked at the eight before any reader had them and found nothing to mend, and no picture was built again after a reading.

Every forced event was read, twenty-four of twenty-four. That is a count of what a reader wrote about a picture built to show the event; it is not the screen, where a scorer who has not seen the picture marks each item against the description. What the readers wrote:
- **The game of catch,** four times, and the thrower the thrower in all four: "has just thrown a red ball (a dashed line shows its flight from her hand) towards a man in a red shirt and blue trousers". Two of the four add the other way round and set it aside: "but the dash trail starting at her hand favours her throwing."
- **The square wheel,** square in all four and no reel, with a hose in two of the pictures: "The wheelbarrow's wheel is a square frame (with a cross in it) instead of a round wheel."
- **The bread:** "With his other hand he holds out a piece of bread to a white duck".
- **The lost balloon,** escaped in all three: "Its string dangles loose and is not attached to anything." Whose it was is still asked, in two of three: "but from this picture alone you can't tell whether it was ever hers."
- **The painter's tin:** "a paint tin stands on the grass at his feet."
- **The stopped hose,** v0.50's drawing: "It could be read as stopping the water (so the woman checks the nozzle), or the dog may simply be standing beside the hose by chance."

Nothing was mended after the readings; each remark went to the screen's list.
screen:
Across all 102 pictures 1,067 of 1,114 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.50: 946 of 992, one). Of the 47 under full marks:
- forty-four are setting items that eight readers left out, thirty-three the clouds and eleven a tree, all zeros (v0.50 had thirty-five, from six readers). Two readers left the clouds out of all eight of their pictures, a third out of seven and a fourth out of six;
- two are the stopped hose's, half marks in one picture: "Whether the brown dog is actually standing on the hose (blocking the water) or just standing next to it; its back feet are right at the hose.";
- one is an ice cream's, a half mark: "She may be looking at the ice cream, or about to lick it."

The set's headline is all items 0.976 (0.949 in v0.50). Of its 287 items eight are under full marks: the clouds in six pictures, which their readers left out (things 0.944, from 0.911), and the stopped hose's two half marks in the tier-3 garden (actions 0.996, inferences 0.985 and contradictions 1.00, from 0.980, 0.953 and 0.942).

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.52 is `vision/flaws_v051.md`.

**The game of catch.** Five pictures: a teenager throwing to a woman, a child to a man twice, and a child to a child twice. The thrower is the thrower in all five: "In the centre a boy in a red cap, blue top and dark trousers has just thrown a red ball (a dotted line shows its path) towards a woman in a yellow dress, who stands with her hands up ready to catch it." Two of the five readers add the other way round among the things they are unsure of, and set it aside: "it could also be read as the man having thrown it to her, but the girl's outstretched arm suggests she threw it." The scorer of that picture listed both of its marks as calls.

**The square wheel.** Eight pictures, four of the bicycle and four of the wheelbarrow, where v0.50 had one of the barrow and failed on it. The wheel is square in all eight, and no reader has a reel: "Under the clothesline sits a grey wheelbarrow whose wheel is square instead of round, which is impossible." Three of the eight name it only among the things they are unsure of, and the scorers listed those marks as calls: "The wheelbarrow's wheel is drawn as a square frame with crossed spokes rather than a round wheel, which looks odd."

**The cast in the descriptions.** By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the four grown figures of v0.49's count are called by a young name first in 5 of their 85 pictures (3 of 79 in v0.50, 20 of 89 in v0.49): the woman in purple in 3 of 25, the woman in the yellow dress in none of 23, the man in the red shirt in 2 of 12 and the man in green in none of 25. The woman in purple is a girl sweeping, walking with an ice cream and pointing at the storm; the man in the red shirt is a boy reading on the bench and sweeping. The man in green has a beard in his line in 14 of his 25 pictures (16 of 20). The moustache of the man in the red shirt is in his line in 1 of 12 (7 of 23), and the older man's in none of 19. Every animal is named for what it is. The teenager is a boy in every item the scorers listed for him; he is one, and the key's word is the scorer's to match.

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers listed 95 full marks as judgement calls, for 82 in v0.50's 90 pictures. In 44 the target stands beside another reading (33 in v0.50), and in 51 a near word or a target partly said was credited (49), twenty-three of them a word for a person. With the 44 halved, eight templates fall under 0.9, and 56 of the 64 pass: `dog_sleeping` and `plant_flowers` (0.7, on five items each), `floating_box` (0.722), `cat_stalks_bird` and `windy_hat` (0.833), `dog_wants_walk` (0.85), `rake` (0.875) and `bird_steals` (0.889). With all 95 halved, 42 pass (35 in v0.50). The scorers gave 13, three, 21 and ten items under full marks, of 282, 290, 293 and 249.

**A retest inside the screen.** Six of the 102 pictures are v0.50's to the pixel: two set pictures, three probes and the tier-4 isomorph. Of their 71 items, 70 have the score they had in v0.50 from other readers and scorers, and one went down, the clouds of a probe.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 32 oddities in the 102 pictures, 0.3 a picture for v0.50's 0.4, and 6 of them in the set for 13. The readers' remarks were 2.59 a picture (2.72 in v0.50). What the remarks are about: a figure drawn in front of what it sits on, in five pictures, on the swing, the slide, the seesaw twice and the bench; figures over the pond's near edge, in four; whose the lost balloon is, in three; and leaves or a wind with no source, in four.
redrawn: `play_catch` and `square_wheel`, which failed v0.50's gate at 0.80 and 0.875, read 1.00 in five and eight pictures. `ducks_bread` reads 1.00 in five pictures, from 0.944 in three, and `lost_balloon` and `paint_fence` 1.00 as before. `blocked_hose`, benched with its swelling short of the paw and left, reads 0.95 again on two half marks in one picture. `bird_steals`, looked at and left, reads 1.00 in six pictures, from 0.90 in five, with four of its eighteen marks beside a second reading: a pass that its drawing did not earn. `ice_cream` has the screen's one other half mark, 0.967 in fifteen pictures. `floating_box`, `cat_stalks_bird`, `dog_sleeping`, `plant_flowers` and `dog_wants_walk` read 1.00 and are the lowest on the strict count. It is one screen, of 3 to 24 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.17.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (30 in three, 12 in four, 16 in five, 2 in six, and one each in eight, nine, fifteen and nineteen). All 64 pass, where 62 did in v0.50, 64 in v0.49 and 63 in v0.48 and in v0.47. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. Two are under 1.00: `blocked_hose` (0.95 on twenty items in five pictures) and `ice_cream` (0.967 on fifteen items in fifteen pictures); the other 62 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v051/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 44 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 56 of the 64 pass. A full gate has been followed by failures before, v0.49's by v0.50's two. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: Four of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where 44 had in v0.50, and all four are `lost_balloon`'s inference (s from -1.071 to -1.118): its child stands where the string's end is clear of the fence's rails. The cast's three poses and revision 48's other rules moved nothing that the calibration measures, and the planner's priors moved with that one line. Seven of the sixteen cells have v0.50's templates; the other nine are new sets, since a set also follows the order in which templates are placed and the sky they may share, and revision 48 changed both. The calibration was measured once, with the cast and the rules as they are released.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 48. Tiers 1 to 3 placed on their showcase seeds; seven of the sixteen cells have v0.50's templates and nine are new sets, and two set pictures are v0.50's to the pixel. The tier-4 park, street and playground placed on v0.50's seeds with v0.50's templates, the street and the playground in another layout, since the square-wheeled bicycle is placed last now. The tier-4 garden placed on v0.50's base at its twenty-sixth step with other templates: v0.50's set had the stopped hose under storm clouds. The isomorphs are five: two of tier 2, two of tier 3 and one of tier 4, the last on v0.50's seed, third call, and identical to v0.50's. The probe pass built 66 and left one template short, the begging dog; three small forced groups filled it, the pass stratified by angle added 9, and three more were forced for the wheelbarrow, which the passes cannot count (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 81 probes, 48 gardens, 21 parks, 10 playgrounds and 2 streets. **I looked at every picture on sheets before any reader had it, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 102 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 387 of 387. Its soft palette warning is raised by 340 records (329 of 385 in v0.50), with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
